name: Prisovex
subcategory: sensory amplifier — visual and auditory enhancement
description: Prisovex is a synthetic terpene-peptide compound that temporarily upregulates the brain's primary sensory cortices, making visual input richer, more saturated, and more dimensionally complex while simultaneously sharpening auditory resolution to near-superhuman levels. Colors become architectural. Music becomes physical. Helix markets it experimentally under a 'sensory wellness' license but it is primarily used recreationally at music events and art installations.
effects: colors perceived as 2-3x more saturated and spatially deep
music perceived as full-body tactile experience
enhanced pattern recognition in visual field
heightened emotional response to aesthetic stimuli
side_effects: music or visual 'echoes' persisting after drug clears
migraine risk in users with ocular augments
rare: permanent upregulation causing chronic sensory overwhelm
cultural_context: Prisovex is the drug of the GLMZ underground music scene — concert halls in Tier 2 industrial districts where sound systems are built to pair with it. Artists and musicians use it to work, claiming it lets them hear what they're actually making. Tier 3 creatives take it to galleries. It's considered relatively 'soft' by recreational standards, which makes its rare permanent side effects easy to dismiss until someone ends up in a sensory clinic.
story_hooks: A sound designer for a Spire entertainment company has been using Prisovex daily for two years — her work is extraordinary but she can no longer function in silence
A Tier 2 venue is selling Prisovex-laced drinks without disclosure; three patrons with ocular augments are now hospitalized with retinal feedback burns
An underground art collective is creating installations specifically designed to cause the rare permanent upregulation — they consider it transcendence, not damage
